## Engineering organization

The client now constructs feature instances and their backing stores in the
application composition root. React Providers and bound commands use the same
instances; endpoint replacement, draft/focus leases, and command retirement remain
with their existing owners. Small Chat/Composer/navigation features keep cohesive
files together, and the native bridge is generated from the actual DesktopHost
method surface and pure Go DTOs. See `ARCHITECTURE.md` for the current structure.
This engineering change preserves the task qualifications and historical receipts
below. The latest resumed goal restores verified batch publication to main.

## Implemented foundation to retain

The built-in Light and Dark schemes keep achromatic canvas, drawer, surface,
elevated, sunken, neutral text and boundary roles. Accent changes cannot advance
those values. `features/theme/kit/scale.ts` now mixes only the theme's declared
canvas/ink and the existing scheme/contrast steps; there is no tint parameter or
second neutral writer. The approved Flame Orange and accent/status roles retain
their meanings, while custom/package palettes keep their own canvas and ink.
`globals.css`, the HTML bootstrap and the native opening window mirror the same
neutral canvases. A remembered built-in background from the tinting release
cannot repaint the first frame; custom/package paint projections remain valid.

The reported recurrence was real: `75fd5dd80` explicitly removed automatic tint
at the user's request, but `d345239c4` later restored it in `neutralScale` and
asserted that behavior in a test. Later main integrations retained it. The
regression is repaired at the scale owner rather than hidden by a page override.

### Startup connection recovery

The actual production Wails entry at published `0c9069714` can leave the main
workspace blank when its isolated Runtime origin is unavailable. Connection
settings has the failure, but the ordinary recovery notice lives inside the
Composer, which ChatPanel does not mount before its Session query finishes.

ChatPanel now retains its existing workspace frame and Conversation region while
waiting for the first defined Session snapshot. The existing
`RuntimeConnectionNotice` is shared with FloatingComposer, with the same service,
localized copy, roles, command and motion. Once a snapshot exists, including a
known empty list, the ordinary Conversation/Composer owns the notice. Explicit
workspace views remain reachable while waiting; Session-owned material and the
ordinary Dock toggle wait for their existing owner to become available. There is
no synthetic Session, draft, request state, retry loop or focus transition.

The first candidate still treated query `isLoading` as readiness. Native retries
repeatedly replaced its recovery button and dropped keyboard focus to BODY; the
same entry briefly painted a false new conversation. Passive Element identities
and direct focus/key observations established real replacement rather than a
CUA selector problem. A new failing regression captures request activity changing
without any Session snapshot. Readiness now follows snapshot existence, so
loading/idle/retry transitions cannot remount that recovery task. The production
query and Runtime lifecycle remain unchanged.

### Control contrast across surfaces

Palette themes derive required control boundaries and focus against the canvas,
drawer, surface, elevated and sunken backgrounds they actually emit. Those five
colors are computed once in `kit/palette.ts` and reused by the emitted tokens and
contrast check. `controlEdge` and `focusRing` replace the retired canvas-only
helpers; `legibleMix` accepts readonly adjacent planes and chooses the first
permitted whole-percentage mix meeting every pair. Existing readable accents,
nonzero floors and saturation at the declared ink remain intact. Light stylesheet
mirrors become focus `#d86231` and edge `#868686`; dark mirrors edge `#6d6d6d`
and retains Orange focus. Neutral planes, text/accent/status ramps, CTA
fill/hover/ink, preferences, Runtime and command behavior retain their owners.

The native task exposes a second owner: a filled control can inherit an inset
focus perimeter that disappears into its own fill. Shared primary `Button`,
checked `Checkbox` and both `Switch` states now project `data-focus-outset`.
The document focus rule honors that marker ahead of an ancestor's inset rule,
keeping its existing 1.5 px perimeter and 1 px outer gap on the surrounding
surface. Unfilled controls/readers retain their inset behavior. There is no
additional ink token, consumer override, product event listener or focus state.
The shared UI README records this responsibility.

Read-only HeroUI theme variables separate surface, field and focus roles.
[Radix's scale guidance](https://www.radix-ui.com/colors/docs/palette-composition/understanding-the-scale)
distinguishes interactive backgrounds from boundaries and focus. [WCAG 2.2
1.4.11](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/non-text-contrast.html)
requires meaningful control/state contrast against adjacent colors. Flame keeps
its own tokens and primitives. Better-colors and better-accessibility guide
actual pair measurement and keyboard evidence; existing layout, typography,
writing and polish research supplies the EN/ZH, 14/18 px, 320 px and 200% review.
No copy, artwork, decorative stripe or motion is added.

### Settings focus and pointer activation

**Behavior and ownership**

At 18 px/200%, native focus could reveal a settings control while leaving its
visible label above the clipped body. `Panel.keepBodyFocusVisible` recognized
wrapping native labels, but `SettingRow` and `FormGroup` compose labels and
controls in a div. Adding local scroll handlers would duplicate the shared
geometry owner.

Those existing roots now declare `data-focus-unit`. Panel selects the nearest
native label or explicit unit and reveals the whole unit when it fits below the
actual clipped viewport, sticky controls and disclosure header. Taller units
retain the existing focused-control fallback. Shared scroll margins use the same
clearance tokens. The application/group declares the reading boundary; Panel
alone decides visibility. There is no preference, semantic label, ARIA, Runtime,
dependency or public API change.

Native pointer QA rejected the first candidate: revealing a row during pointer
focus moved the font trigger between pointerdown and pointerup, swallowing its
first click. Panel retains only the pending pressed Element until pointerup or
cancellation. A press on that control, its child, wrapping native label or existing
slider focus proxy leaves activation at the pressed position, including reflow
during the press. Unrelated programmatic autofocus still reveals its own field;
leaving the body clears the press. Keyboard/programmatic reveal and geometry
changes retain the same shared path. No global modality owner, timer, retry,
pointer capture or prevented native event is added.

This follows better-accessibility's visible-focus/200% guidance and
better-layout's complete reading groups, retaining the existing component and
focus-model research above. The row-label finding is a reading-context problem;
the original control itself was named and reachable. It is not presented as a
newly measured WCAG failure or whole-product award qualification. Typography,
spacing, colors, motion and skins stay with their existing owners.

| ------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| MEDIUM                         | ui/settings/SettingRow.tsx; packages/ui/src/panel.tsx | Focus can expose a control without its visible label                                         | Fitting label/control units reveal together; tall units retain the control fallback | Preserve the current decision's reading context at large type/zoom |
| MEDIUM                         | packages/ui/src/panel.tsx, FormGroup                  | Composite form groups lack the same reveal boundary                                          | Shared FormGroup declares its existing complete reading unit                        | Keep a transport choice and its group name together                |
| HIGH, resolved before delivery | packages/ui/src/panel.tsx                             | The initial candidate moves a trigger during pointer activation and consumes the first click | Causally related pointer focus keeps the pressed position; keyboard reveal remains  | A visible menu trigger must respond to its first click             |

**Production viewport reflow qualification (2026-10-28)**

This follow-up starts from published `9014e9689` and confirms the color batch's
remaining focus finding against the complete production Web entry and actual
Wails bootstrap. The registered Settings page uses Panel without a controls
slot. Panel previously observed only its own controls, so the production owner
had no geometry notification when the viewport changed around an already focused
field. Adding a local Appearance scroll effect would leave the shared cause.

Panel now observes its content, controls and clipped host ancestors; native window
resize also rechecks its reading frame. The original focused Element is the
reading witness. Reflow reveals its nearest fitting label/unit, or the control's
beginning when the unit is too tall, through the existing scroll path. No focus,
input, selection, draft or preference transition is synthesized. Native fractional
scroll edges use a half-CSS-pixel tolerance. An oversized field whose beginning
is visible stays still.

A wheel gesture retires follow. A moved scrollbar that leaves the field behind
does too; a zero-displacement notification or changed frame can instead precede
native reflow and keeps the witness. Later outside focus, inactive retained
content and unmount retire it. The original controls-height projection remains
independent of retained visibility. Pointerup/cancellation retires the pending
press, and reflow cannot move the pressed control before activation finishes.
Existing feedback and Disclosure callers retain the same Panel context contract;
the transcript reading owner is unchanged.

### Paper texture and reading surfaces

Appearance offers Off, Xuan paper, Cotton paper and Fine grain through the existing
Segmented control. Strength uses the shared Slider from 1 to 5 and retains its
value across Off and restart. Existing installations start with Off and strength
3; valid older appearance records retain their other settings. Both paper fields
participate in settings search. New rows use labels without helper copy, and
SettingRow no longer reserves space for an absent description.

The user's paper reference defines this optional material and strength task.
Its unrelated stickers, sunlight and tree controls are not added. After the
user reported that the first effect was too faint, the material became visibly
stronger at the middle setting. Xuan combines distributed fibers and grain;
Cotton and Fine grain use distinct fixed noise fields. Existing HeroUI/Radix
surface-role research and the better-accessibility, layout, writing, typography,
colors and UI reviews guide the controls, reading planes and verification.
Approved branding and artwork remain intact; no colored decorative stripe or
new motion is added.

One appearance preference owns the choice and strength. The document painter
publishes a static seamless 512 px SVG image through --surface-texture and marks
the root while paper is enabled. Shared Panel/sticky controls, settings rail/page,
workspace viewport, conversation scroll viewport and the actual opaque sidebar
face enroll at their surface owners. There is no overlay, animation, text filter,
extra input handler or new dependency. Off removes the enrollment marker so it
cannot mask an existing visual-style background image. Fields, menus and record
cards retain their existing fills. Forced colors suppress the image.

Grain opacity and Xuan fiber opacity have one owner in kit/paperTexture.ts.
The same owner supplies the maximum combined opacity to the existing palette
algorithm, which checks the painted canvas/drawer/surface bounds in addition to
plain planes. Both built-in and public contributed palette producers update
text, control edges and focus when paper or strength changes. The neutral plane
colors, main text, solid accent/CTA and Off-state tokens are unchanged. Custom
theme scheme changes repaint the material through the existing contribution
subscription. No competing contrast state or correction layer is added.

### Image gallery selection and source geometry

Reading a reply → opening its image → changing or zooming the selection → closing
→ continuing the original draft is now qualified in native fullscreen. This
supersedes the old beta.29 production-fixture fullscreen qualification gap below;
the historical visibility contradiction remains evidence about that old scene.
Current beta.34 reaches visible, focused fullscreen with advancing frame callbacks
both from an ordinary window and from the public fullscreen startup condition.
Temporary hidden frames during the native transition are excluded.

**Cause and ownership**

- The original `ImageInspector key={gallery.index}` remounted the pan area and
  zoom controls on every selection. Actual native ArrowRight from Zoom in left
  focus on BODY, still there in the next independent observation. The existing
  lightbox Portal now owns the inspector's open lifetime. Captured `GalleryItem`
  identity resets viewing state, including distinct entries sharing one URI;
  controls and the pan area keep their nodes and focus.
- The current item owns its fitted dimensions; another item's dimensions never
  render onto its new image. Its source owns the displayed image element. The
  existing resize lifecycle cancels a drag and resets fit/scroll as before.
- Native acceptance rejected two intermediate sizing approaches. Re-reading the
  displayed SVG's natural dimensions fed fitted/zoomed output back into input;
  a later per-visible-image cache still doubled a 240 × 96 source after switching
  away and back at page 200%. In the same native scene a detached decoder read
  240 × 96 at page 100%, 150% and 200%, while the rendered element's readout
  followed CSS size and page zoom. The final current-item lifecycle owns one
  detached browser Image resource, installs its load handler before assigning
  the source, measures that source and removes the handler on selection/close.
  It is never appended to the document. This removes the competing dimension
  owner without parsing SVG, guessing page zoom, adding hidden images or retrying
  focus/animation. The independent native observations establish this host's
  behavior; [WebKit's image sizing implementation](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebCore/html/HTMLImageElement.cpp)
  and [Apple's pageZoom contract](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/webkit/wkwebview/pagezoom)
  supplied implementation context, not substitutes for those observations.
- `ImagePreviewGallery.tsx` is the only changed product file. Existing modal
  completion, shared controls, image save, theme, Runtime and command owners
  remain in place. No dependency, locale, asset, storage or native preference
  changes are needed.

### Conversation import file reads

A selected file could fail to read without any visible result. The native Wails
baseline selects an owned `unreadable.json` with POSIX mode `000`: the actual
`File.text()` rejects with `NotReadableError: The I/O read operation failed.`,
but the adapter resolves `null`, which the application correctly interprets as
cancellation. No Runtime import or error notification follows. The original
textarea and its draft survive. This is a real filesystem read failure, with no
injected exception or simulated picker.

**Ownership and resulting behavior**

- `adapters/fileTransfer.ts` has one once-only settlement/cleanup path for text,
  cancellation and rejection. Cancel or an empty selection resolves `null`;
  successful text, including an empty string, remains exact; a failed read
  rejects with its original cause. Saving through the composed host is unchanged.
- `application/conversationExport.ts` handles the selection/read stage inside
  its existing generation. A current failure publishes `convExport.readFailed`
  through the established import notification source. Retired work stays quiet.
  The existing operation promise still owns repeated intent and releases the next
  explicit import. JSON parsing, Runtime admission, rehydration, collection repair
  and selection/success keep their established contracts.
- All eight locale files add the read-failure message and give the existing
  invalid-JSON and import-failure messages a concrete recovery step. Raw
  filesystem/Runtime diagnostics remain outside user-facing text. No new host
  method, picker, busy state, retry mechanism, error hierarchy, style or theme
  owner was introduced.

The [File API text algorithm](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#blob-text) preserves
read rejections, and its [read-error contract](https://w3c.github.io/FileAPI/#dfn-error-codes)
covers unreadable underlying storage. The
[HTML input cancellation event](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLInputElement/cancel_event)
describes user cancellation separately. ZCode's actual
`packages/desktop/src/main/desktopMainIpcPlatform.ts:118–150` similarly keeps
cancelled native selection separate from selected paths; it supplies no Flame
read-generation policy. HeroUI's actual
`apps/docs/src/demos/en/toast/promise.tsx` and `toast/variants.tsx` separate
failure feedback from successful work and name a recovery action. Flame retains
its existing notification, reader, theme and source-return owners.

### Retained component behavior

| Product area                  | Current behavior and ownership                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Shared presentation           | Panels, persistent controls, resource groups, disclosures, forms, modal geometry, metric summaries and semantic badges share presentation owners. The host owns appearance values; `/Users/tangerg/Desktop/flame/ui` owns reusable presentation rules. Pages compose those rules.                                                                              |
| Color and brand               | The default accent is Flame Orange. Built-in page planes, neutral ink and boundaries stay achromatic across accent changes. Content emphasis keeps its semantic accent roles; custom themes retain their own colors and the approved brand assets remain.                                                                                                      |
| Prose and layout              | Prose takes one reading step above interface text: 16 px with the default 14 px interface, while code keeps its separate preference. Paragraphs use one gap; headings have unitless leading and a visible following gap, including deeper levels. The `65ch` cap and wider code/table/media measures remain intentional.                                       |
| Markdown tables               | Long tables stay within a bounded reading viewport. Compact table actions follow the table edge and wrap when necessary. Expanded previews keep controls and column headings reachable. Do not reintroduce page overflow or remove access to long data.                                                                                                        |
| Code and recorded output      | One stable bounded code-reading region retains literal selection, scroll and focus as syntax highlighting arrives. Shared captions, wrapping and copy behavior are established. Loading messages no longer expose raw Markdown source as a temporary presentation.                                                                                             |
| Selection and file references | Ordinary action-button drags cannot select the surrounding application. Reading text and inline file references remain selectable. Dragging a file reference preserves selection without navigating the Dock; ordinary clicks and Enter/Space still open its path and line. Native copy and whitespace dismissal work.                                         |
| Tool rows                     | Rows reserve action space only when real actions exist. Recorded paths wrap at directory boundaries and retain literal copy. Expanded groups remain visible and clickable as the Dock narrows; the WebKit grid sizing repair preserves reversible transitions.                                                                                                 |
| MCP configuration drafts      | The mounted editor owns feedback and view completion. Existing MCP commands retain their captured inputs, Runtime generation and cache-repair owner. Pending field/control presentation comes from the shared primitives; import identity validation completes before command admission.                                                                       |
| Context Dock                  | File identity and return navigation precede a separate wrapping mode/action row. Full directories remain available beneath the filename. Opening from the tree focuses the return action; returning restores the tree cursor without stealing another region's focus. Panels grow through their complete content; fixed pane seams paint above child surfaces. |
| Subagent stop controls        | Shared filled stop marks and quiet circular controls replace the checkbox-like outline squares. Their placement is consistent across the narrative, Dock list and detail view; terminal entries reserve no dead cancel slot.                                                                                                                                   |
| Main and delegated messages   | Both use `MessageTranscript` for ordered turns, dates, reading gutters and isolated recovery, with shared `MessageTurn` / `MessageBlock` content and actions. Child rows retain their own Run and referenced facts. Their overview keeps its scroll position; returning restores the originating task's focus.                                                 |
| Motion and focus              | Shared moving item backplates remain interruptible and reversible and consume the host motion tokens. Reduced motion, scoped code Select All, native dismissal and focus return have established owners and regression coverage.                                                                                                                               |
| Authoring and acceptance      | One captured submission owns draft consumption and history. Rejected input stays editable; delayed acceptance preserves successor revisions, Session changes, attachment staging and other controls' focus. Goal and slash extensions share this settlement contract.                                                                                          |

File-reference gesture behavior lives in `/Users/tangerg/Desktop/flame/apps/web/src/features/chat/file-references/public/FileRefLink.tsx`: pointer activation consults the browser's existing selection; keyboard activation remains available. The native scrolling background defect came from shared `Panel` roots shrinking
inside a column flex viewport: long children overflowed below the panel's canvas
and sticky-control boundary. `Panel` now opts out of that shrinking. The weak Dock
separation had a different cause: the inset seam painted beneath opaque child
reading surfaces. The conversation plane's fixed edge now paints the same
full-plane inset wash as the left sidebar edge, without a persistent
dark stroke or additional hover/drag darkening. Both edges share one wash rule;
the resize cursor and keyboard focus treatment remain available. Do not cover
either defect with per-view background patches or duplicate dividers.

Main and selected-subagent views now compose one `MessageTranscript`. It owns
ordered turns, stable keys, neighbors, date separators, reading gutters and
per-turn render recovery. `MessageTurn` and `MessageBlock` continue to own message
content and actions. Agent's existing fact slicer projects each child message for
that common renderer, so
running siblings do not suppress a finished child's actions. The same streaming
preference applies in both narratives. Copy and feedback retain the selected
message identity; regeneration appears only for a main-conversation message that
the existing replay operation can locate. Main and child scroll following remain
independent, while sharing the reading-focus guard and latest-content control.
Jumping to the bottom transfers focus to that reader before hiding the control.
The running-status pill keeps one line and grows with text size instead of
wrapping outside a fixed-height background under narrow-window pressure.

turn boundary, so one message failure replaced the complete Subagents panel.
`TurnErrorBoundary` now lives beside the common transcript. Its Retry action
retires focus inside the disappearing fallback into the nearest existing reader
before resetting; already-outside focus and recovered content's own focus still
win. The error logging policy added on current `main` remains one implementation
in `ui/atoms/logging-error-boundary.tsx`, shared with `ChatErrorBoundary`.

`MessageStream` retains the main scroll/follow host and selects the terminal Run

`SubagentsPanel` retains each Run's independent reader, retained hidden content,
selection and source chain. Both consume the same transcript, without a renderer

and public `MessageTurn` entry are removed; all in-scope callers are migrated.

says; it must not be replaced with counts of the local matches. Native baseline
confirms a different problem: an empty match only instructs the reader to clear

style, new abstraction, read, command or optimistic record is added. Paging,
accepted snapshots, revisions, modal tasks and original receipt owners remain
authoritative. Only Schedules' published component ESM changes; the other ten
resources retain their bytes. No persisted-data or protocol migration is needed.

## Global Composer focus and retained material

The existing `composer.focus` command belongs to the installed workbench. Its ID,
localized label, Mod-L binding and stored shortcut-override identity are unchanged.
The plugin installation owns one React ref to `ChatPanel`'s small imperative
handle; no global handler registry was added. The obsolete single-export panel
index has no consumers and is removed. Other default commands retain their owner.

`useInspectionFocus` handles the explicit request before its generic presentation
focus. A visible Composer receives ordinary local input focus without navigation.
For a hidden conversation, one ref-owned request captures the Session, active
element, inspection and expected Dock location. An immutable token ensures a
commit even when later navigation coalesces back to the old route. Delivery is
one-shot and requires a visible conversation, unchanged scope and still-unclaimed
focus. A later control/region, replacement Session or superseding navigation
retires the request; unmounting retains no deferred callback. An active dialog
keeps its task boundary. No timeout, retry, forced flush or region fallback was
added.

one existing navigation operation. A narrow inspection can therefore reveal the
conversation without the inspection immediately projecting full width again.
The view and optional Dock change form one history entry; stored tabs, queries,
file targets and inspection ancestry remain with their existing owners. Ordinary
selection, Close and notification callers keep the default preserve policy.

owner. Its main presentation uses the active location or the existing
`dockTabToShow` memory policy, with the catalog for an empty Dock. The host no
longer guesses the first tab or a default Files view. This completes explicit
inspection → focus/continue drafting → reopen the same material, as well as
history Back. The established low-level Composer focus, captured acceptance
return, draft and submit ports remain unchanged; asynchronous acceptance does not
gain this explicit navigation behavior. No Runtime or stored schema changed.

### Selection quote placement, keyboard access and dismissal

The placement repair remains intact. The original English action measured
**55.4 × 106 px** near the right edge and began at **y = -10 px** above an upper
paragraph. `SelectionQuote.tsx` now supplies the complete native range rectangle
to the existing Popover positioner: fixed placement, a 6 px gap, viewport
collisions and content-driven width. `ui/atoms/popover.tsx` forwards these existing
capabilities and permits a surface-free container; ordinary Popovers retain their
panel. The raised Button remains the sole visible surface. Native multi-click
extension in the same source remains valid, while scroll, resize, outside
activation and completion retire the local action and queued selection refresh.

The keyboard gap was independently reproduced in actual Wails on both the
original `05efd8213` source and placement baseline `32a3e4fd3`: native Tab from the
selected paragraph focused its next file link, collapsed the selection and
removed Quote. A virtual positioning anchor is not a real Popover trigger or a
focus-order bridge. SelectionQuote now handles only explicit, unmodified forward
Tab from the active source's reader scope and focuses its real button. The
captured quote can survive WebKit collapsing selection only while that keyboard
task owns button focus and its original source remains valid.

The same pending task retains exact range boundaries and DOM material for
validation, plus the existing reader element for local return. The rendered
Selection text remains the quote payload: native paragraph selection measured
**176 characters**, while its DOM Range serialized **175**. Those different
separator contracts are not interchangeable. A changed range, file identity,
hidden/disconnected source, later focus or modal task retires the old operation
without quoting stale material or clearing somebody else's selection. Source
validity is checked on subsequent selection, key and activation events; this does
not promise immediate eventless-unmount notification.

Tab, Shift+Tab or Escape from the keyboard-entered action returns to the existing
reader with `preventScroll`, retires only its own remaining selection and leaves
the next Tab to normal document order. Ordinary selection Escape keeps its
previous scope and preserves the selected text. Activation clears the quote task
before using the existing Composer append/reveal owner; it adds no competing
Composer focus policy. Native WebKit focused the button without matching
`:focus-visible`, so the button uses the established `data-focus-proxy` contract
only during this keyboard task. The shared keyboard-modality gate, semantic focus
color, radius and outline remain authoritative. No shared CSS, dependency,
Runtime, protocol, persisted-data or locale migration is required.

Read-only ZCode `SelectionActionMenu.tsx` and `ConversationSelectionTooltip.tsx`
provide placement and source-scope evidence, but their collapsed-selection
behavior does not establish a working keyboard entry path. HeroUI's actual
Popover separates placement from dialog semantics; Arc's Popover supplies compact
offsets and collision insets. ChatGPT's actual selected-text overlay preserves
pointer selection and does not establish keyboard reachability. The installed
Base UI focus manager confirms that its virtual anchor supplies geometry without
a real trigger focus target. The official
[Base UI Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover),
[Radix Popover](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/popover) and
[WCAG keyboard guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/keyboard.html)
inform the explicit local focus task. Better-accessibility and better-layout guide
visible focus, normal exit and retained reading geometry.

### Continue writing after a selection quote

The native keyboard acceptance above exposed a formatting defect: immediate
continuation joined the closing file fence or final blockquote line. Rendering
the unchanged `475555981` formatter with the installed Markdown parser confirms
that the new writing becomes quoted material. `quoteText` now adds one blank
paragraph after each message, file or tool-output quote. This is the single owner
of the fragment's Markdown boundary; the existing append owner still joins draft
parts and requests Composer focus. It trims the previous part before another
append, so consecutive quotes do not accumulate separators. Send-intent trimming
keeps quote-only body/history unchanged and preserves a continued paragraph.
No UI event, focus, source identity, dependency, Runtime, protocol or persisted
data contract changes are needed.

Read-only ZCode `ConversationComposer.tsx` renders quote-reference chips separately
from its plain message text, supporting a clear distinction between source
material and the user's writing; Flame retains its existing Markdown contract.
ChatGPT's actual selected-text overlay establishes pointer selection handling,
not a newline policy. The official CommonMark
[fenced-code](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/#fenced-code-blocks) and
[blockquote](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/#block-quotes) rules explain why a
continuation on the closing-fence line invalidates that fence and why an
unseparated paragraph can remain inside a blockquote. Better-writing and
better-typography guide this readable source/writing boundary; better-accessibility
guides continuity through the existing keyboard and focus path.

### Preserve Markdown fences inside quoted files

The canonical README source contains a fenced TypeScript example on lines
**17–19**. On unchanged `8322a31fd`, actual native selection and quote activation
wrap that example in another three-backtick fence. Rendering the resulting
fragment with the installed Markdown parser produces two code blocks and consumes
the user's continuation as code. The formatter now chooses at least three
backticks and one more than the longest contiguous backtick run in the body.
File and tool-output fragments share that framing rule in `quoteText`; message
quoting, file path/line labels, trailing-body trimming and the final blank
paragraph retain their contracts. No selection, focus, draft, Runtime, protocol,
persisted-data or dependency change is required.

The official CommonMark
[fenced-code rule](https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/#fenced-code-blocks)
requires a closing fence to be at least as long as its opener. A longer outer
delimiter therefore keeps the selected markers literal. The read-only ZCode
reference above supports separating source material from the user's writing;
it does not supply this Markdown implementation. Better-writing and
better-typography guide that distinction, and better-accessibility guides the
unchanged keyboard and return path. The separate message-footer review confirms
that `MessageBlock` places actions and its terminal footer outside the quote
source. Cross-boundary retirement is expected; no footer repair is justified.

## Search selection and task handoff

`src/ui/atoms/search-overlay.tsx` owns the end of the bounded search task before
handing its selected action to a destination. Pointer and Enter selection capture
one callback and request controlled closure. Base UI's close completion publishes
an immutable token; a committed effect consumes the callback from its sole ref
owner after modal isolation cleanup. The retained intent prevents a later
primitive return-focus job from overriding the selected destination. Repeated
activation during closing cannot dispatch the choice twice, and unmounting
retires a choice that has not been delivered.

If the closing surface still owns focus, the surviving opener is restored before
the action runs. A local command such as Toggle theme therefore retains context,
and an action can intentionally focus a destination or open another search task
from that same origin. Later outside focus remains authoritative for cancellation
and non-focusing actions. Ordinary dismissal executes no choice. CommandMenu and
SessionSearch retain only their existing command/session callbacks; the shared
surface now owns their close request. Query/highlight resets, matching, row
announcements, keyboard/IME handling and visual tokens retain their established
contracts. Business command, Session, navigation and Runtime owners are unchanged.

Read-only research inspected ZCode's actual
`command-center/CommandCenterDialog.tsx` and
`quickpick/QuickPickCommandDialog.tsx`: both request closure before handing
the selected command or task to its owner. Their immediate callbacks are task-model
evidence, not proof of Wails focus ordering. Installed Base UI 1.9.0
`FloatingFocusManager.mjs` shows its queued return focus and the explicit-target
exception to its outside-focus guard; `popupStoreUtils.mjs` and
`useUnmountAfterClose.mjs` establish the close-completion/commit distinction.
Flame's existing CatalogPicker supplies a local one-shot handoff precedent, while
the search surface also needs a return for non-focusing commands. Better-series
focus and layout guidance retains the existing modal, semantic surfaces, query
field, reading/list rhythm and Orange/custom-blue focus roles. Existing Radix
Dialog and HeroUI modal references inform the bounded task model; static Ace
artwork supplies no keyboard evidence.

### Find follows rendered reply updates

Find now refreshes its matches when the presented reply changes. An open query
keeps the selected occurrence in its rendered message, updates the stable result
count and replaces collapsed or detached CSS Highlight ranges. The refresh does
not focus, select or reveal anything. Explicit query changes and Next/Previous
remain the owners of match navigation; the existing reading-follow policy keeps
its own scroll decisions.

On frozen base `fe9c0ae4700b880a08fb66faab8eb76bab419d8f`, actual Wails reproduces
**2 / 2** after a third matching chunk arrives. Its two old highlight ranges read
`Search checkpoint` and an empty string. After the captured reply is removed,
the old count stays **2 / 2** and both ranges are empty. The root cause is that
query changes alone built the Range array, although React can replace the text
to which a live Range refers.

`apps/web/src/features/chat/search/adapters/messageRanges.ts:72` now returns
each Range with its rendered message root and local occurrence. The existing
inline-flow, literal, case-insensitive and UTF-16 matching rules remain intact.
Its scoped MutationObserver accepts message text changes and added/removed
message subtrees, ignoring unrelated chrome and Find's own counter. It observes
only while an open nonempty query owns a visible Conversation. Close, clearing,
Session changes and content hiding retire that subscription through the existing
lifetime. No timer, persistent index, Runtime state or competing reply projection
is introduced. All callers migrate to `findMessageMatches`; no obsolete alias
remains.

`apps/web/src/features/chat/search/ui/ChatSearchOverlay.tsx:85` retains the
message/occurrence when it remains, otherwise bounds the previous result index
to the current matches. A native intermediate candidate correctly updates to
**0 / 0**, but natively disabling its focused Next button loses focus to body.
The final Previous/Next controls use the existing `focusableWhenDisabled`
contract. One Find-level capture handler replaces four separate key handlers,
owning Escape and query-only Enter/Shift+Enter before the disabled action guard.
Disabled activation and submission remain with the shared primitive. This
scope boundary also leaves later outside focus with its owner.

Read-only ZCode `useConversationTimelineFind.ts` distinguishes a current match
key from its global index during rendered updates. Its cache, virtualization and
history loading are not copied. HeroUI's actual SearchField composes a controlled
query with native input/group/clear primitives; it does not prove streaming Find
behavior. ChatGPT's actual keyboard-shortcut SearchInput gives its caller first
refusal and keeps Escape local; it is a settings control, not evidence of a
conversation index. Existing Arc/Radix and Ace visual research remains applicable
to scope, restrained hierarchy and return. The missing Ace contact-sheet caches
are not recreated: the original Alpaca and Marketer source pages are reopened
read-only. Static reference images do not qualify keyboard behavior.

## Composer model catalog recovery

`src/features/composer/ui/ModelPicker.tsx` now treats catalog availability separately
from resolution of the current model. When a nonempty catalog cannot resolve the
Session's exact selection, the existing localized Switch model action and neutral
server glyph remain available. Provider and recent groups still contain only
known catalog entries, with no row marked as current. Loading, empty and failed
catalog branches retain their existing behavior.

Integration retains the already-authored primary `main` contract from
`02ac171c8`: an explicit preference carries its provider/model identity even when
catalog metadata is unavailable, and sending reads that preference directly.
Its owner/callers/tests and localized unavailable hint are included as an exact
frontend dependency. Such a preference still displays its original identity,
provider and unavailable hint, including an empty catalog. The neutral action is
reserved for absence of a resolved identity. Choosing a replacement remains an
explicit user decision; this presentation repair does not advance the selection
on its own.

The existing selection resolver still reports unknown when a durable Session's
model is absent, its summary is pending, or a new Session has no Runtime default.
Opening, searching and cancelling the picker do not choose another model or write
a preference. An explicit choice still writes the exact provider/model pair,
remembers that item and keeps a supported prior effort or the selected model's
own default. Once resolved, the trigger, provider scope and current-row treatment
retain their established behavior. An open search also survives loss of the
current selection instead of unmounting with the old loading placeholder.
No new state owner, fallback model, effect, focus workaround, command or wire
contract was introduced.

Read-only research inspected ZCode's actual
`chat-input-toolbar/modelSelection.ts`: trigger display and catalog membership
are distinct concerns. Its `useModelSelectionView.ts` also distinguishes retained
catalog data from a resolved effective selection; its service and retry machinery
were not copied. HeroUI's local `select/controlled.tsx` keeps a nullable controlled
value and a usable placeholder, while `popover/basic.tsx` keeps the bounded task
with its trigger. These support the task model rather than a replacement control
system. Better-writing guidance favors the existing localized action over an
indefinite loading signal; better-accessibility/layout review retains Base UI's
keyboard/focus behavior, shared chip sizing, semantic surfaces and Orange/custom
accent roles. Static Ace references supply no selection or focus evidence.

Provider roles can be known from installed contributions before their independent
selection read succeeds. Previously, that known-role branch bypassed DataView and
hid read failures; an absent selection record was always rendered as unselected.
A refresh failure also retained selected identities without identifying the failed
read. Canonical native counterexamples on frozen base
`98be315eb2ad16cf377e46acfbac7255e27af62e` show two false unselected rows after
initial failure, then selected memory/schedules rows with no failure marker after
a later refresh fails.

`features/plugins/ui/ProviderSelections.tsx` now derives read availability from
its existing query data. Until that query has accepted data, roles say Selection
not read. A successful empty read confirms unselected roles. The existing compact
DataError appears alongside contributed roles on failure; a failed refresh states
that retained identities are the last read. The persistent Refresh selections
control remains the single recovery action in this branch. The no-role DataView
and unsupported-method feedback retain their behavior. Eight existing catalogs
add only the two read-state messages. This is necessary result provenance, not
another instruction, slogan or decorative secondary label.

Installation contributions own candidate availability; the selection query owns
accepted selection facts; each existing ProviderRole owns its candidate draft.
The public client continues to own explicit selection, idempotency, observation
and unknown-outcome recovery. Read failure does not disable a valid explicit
choice, infer a selected candidate or clear a draft. No shared primitive, Runtime,
SDK, transport protocol, storage or dependency changes are required. The existing
Plugins pane introduction is unchanged; this batch does not claim its removal.

for separating candidate configuration from accepted selection; HeroUI’s actual

one persistent action and the existing grouped rows, uses short factual state
copy and preserves the current focus owner. Flame’s Base UI, StyleX, semantic
colors, approved branding, Orange and custom themes retain their owners.

`plugins/trajectory/component/component.tsx` keeps the accepted cursor chain and
captured descendant scope as the sole page identity. Refresh rereads those values;
it no longer silently returns an older-page reader to the newest page. Initial
entry still negotiates scope. The visible status names the accepted page and
record count, with singular/plural wording and an explicit last-accepted label
after failure. Counts and filters remain local to that page; opaque cursors do
not establish a total page count.

navigation origin is consumed after a successful accepted-page commit: the
existing summary receives focus only while the initiating action or unclaimed
document body owns it. Initial reads, refresh, failures, retired reads and later
filter/Composer focus choices do not move it. The existing Panel owns revealing
that focused body below its measured sticky controls; no local scroll mechanism,
timer, competing page state or shared primitive change was needed. Filtering and
same-page refresh preserve surviving record disclosure instances.

and refreshes. A selected Run absent from the accepted page stays in the option

of past Runs or another state transition. The empty-string Session only identity

does not identify image bytes outside the canonical message-content boundary.

objects. Reading and complete raw evidence keep their original records and image
bytes. No state, cache, dependency, style, label, locale or semantic owner is added.

focus, commands and Runtime generation retain their contracts. The former global
key-based replacer is removed; only Trajectory's normal ESM resource changes.
No persisted-data or protocol migration is needed.

## File browsing and keyboard continuity

`apps/web/src/features/workspace/ui/files/FileTree.tsx` retains one stored cursor:
the last row that actually received focus. Its visible keyboard entry is derived
through the currently rendered directory responses. A surviving row keeps the
entry; a hidden or removed descendant uses its nearest visible ancestor; an
absent root uses the first remaining root. Loading and error states use the same
visibility conditions as `DataView`. Collapsing a branch while working elsewhere
keeps that later control's focus and lets the original cursor resume if the
branch reopens without another row receiving focus.

The tree root owns removal focus through its private ref and stable callbacks.
A row reports its retirement before detachment; the replacement only reclaims
focus when that removed row owned it and the document body still has it. Child
rows do not mutate a borrowed ref. Existing preview/back, selected-file identity,
expanded-directory memory, query lifetimes and Runtime filesystem ownership stay
with their existing owners. Initial root loading without accepted nonempty data replaces the entire tree;
this change guarantees a reachable entry on remount, not automatic focus across
that separate loading boundary. Accepted background refreshes now follow the
root-refresh contract below.

`apps/web/src/ui/atoms/tree.tsx` uses the existing `data-focus-proxy` rule.
Actual Wails exposed a pointer-to-arrow path where the active row moved without
WebKit making it `:focus-visible` until a later Tab. The proxy gives that same
row the shared focus ring as soon as the existing document modality owner sees
keyboard navigation. It adds no event listener, palette, focus state or outline
value; pointer focus still follows the established suppression policy.

The existing workspace fixture now names its root `apps`, matching the file paths
after the repository layout change. Its ordinary browser expectations follow
that corrected identity; no browser suite was started. Native refresh controls
and theme links are temporary build transforms, not shipped debug behavior.

`review-file-tree-side-pane-3e6c9e54ce58.js` separates selected file, selected root
and pane width; it is interface code, not an exporter. Flame keeps its existing

and Popover demos, the linked Radix focus and semantic color references above,
and the Ace overviews plus full-size Alpaca tool and Marketer workspace images

this file-browse/read/return flow; unchanged colors, typography and control
surfaces retain their existing owners.

### Native multiline insertion boundary

The task remains source copy → authoring → continue the original draft. The
clipboard contains the exact 93-character Go sample, including CJK, tabs, double
spaces, internal blank lines and two final LF characters. Pasting it into the
single-line `Prefix. ` draft should produce 101 characters. Actual first insertion
produces 100, with one final LF. Passive native Paste and beforeinput observations
retain all 93 clipboard characters; the input event already exposes the loss.

The draft store, Composer input controller and shared TextArea do not trim this
short native paste. The uncontrolled native textarea, controlled textarea, shared
TextArea and autosizing TextArea reproduce the same result. A separate
uncontrolled field has no input observers at all: only an explicit button reads
the committed value after paste, and still reports 100. Two/twelve rows, wrap
off, break-spaces, spellcheck off and the isolated application's Smart Copy/Paste
setting do not repair the default paste. That setting is restored before Quit.

An independent AppKit application uses a default public WKWebViewConfiguration,
ordinary Edit-menu selectors and a static local HTML page. It imports neither
Wails nor React and has no input listeners. Native system paste followed by the
explicit read button reports **100 / expected 101 / one trailing LF**. Native
Undo retains the eight-character prefix; Redo returns the same 100-character
result. This reproduces the boundary on **macOS 26.5 (25F71)**, system WebKit
**21624.2.5.11.4**, independently of Flame and Wails. The Wails probe is built with
SDK 26.5 and deployment target 13.0. It does not establish behavior on another
OS, a newer engine, Safari or Safari Technology Preview, or identify the exact
upstream implementation defect.

Private alternatives are rejected, with no production edits:

| Native insertion experiment                                                                    | Observed result                                                                                                                  | Decision                                              |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `execCommand("insertText")`                                                                    | Retains both LF characters but native smart substitution changes the closing ASCII quote. `autocorrect=off` does not prevent it. | Reject: source text changes.                          |
| Temporarily disable spellcheck around `insertText`, then restore it                            | Exact 101 characters, but one native Undo removes the genuinely typed prefix too, leaving an empty draft; Redo restores 101.     | Reject: paste loses its independent undo transaction. |
| `insertHTML` with a DOM-created preformatted span, textContent, optional final BR, or pre/code | Still 100 characters and one final LF. The ordinary span retains the prefix on Undo.                                             | Reject: does not repair the defect.                   |

There is no extra LF, custom history, value reconciliation, private native API,
global preference change or new editor. Existing short-paste, composition,
attachment, draft and native undo owners remain intact. This is a verified
platform limitation with no safe tested repair, not successful retry acceptance.
Revisit when a supported engine update or native paste API can preserve both
literal content and the independently undoable insertion.

### File-tree hierarchy and selectability

The actual Wails baseline at `26a891365` exposes two separate semantic gaps.
Expanded `apps` and `nested` rows render their child groups as DOM siblings,
without containment or an `aria-owns` association. Each directory also exposes
`aria-selected=false`, although its activation only changes expansion.
Declared level/position/size metadata does not supply the missing ownership.

`FileTree.tsx:97` now derives a group ID from the node's existing React
`useId` stem. The row references that group under the same expansion condition
that mounts it. Collapsed branches and leaves have no owned-group reference;
separate trees with the same paths resolve their own groups. The interactive
row and ContextMenu trigger keep their existing sibling layout. Files retain
their selected/current projection; folders omit selection state.
`ui/primitives/tree.tsx:77` accepts an omitted `selected` value without
inferring selectability from expansion, so a generic caller can still select
branches. The fix adds no mutable state, ref, effect, timer, query policy or
navigation owner.

Read-only ZCode's actual `WorkspaceFileTreeRowView.tsx:213` is useful for
separate row activation and selected-object styling, but its flat row declarations
are not evidence for a complete accessible hierarchy. The normative source is
[WAI's tree pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/):
parent rows contain or own child groups, and nodes that cannot be selected omit
selection state. Existing remembered cursor and selected-file behavior remain
separate; this scope does not add keyboard features or replace the navigation
model. The better-accessibility review is scoped to these declarations and
the exercised keyboard paths.

| Severity | Location                                        | Before                                                       | After                                                                                             | Why                                                                               |
| -------- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| MEDIUM   | `FileTree.tsx:149`, `FileTree.tsx:215`          | Child groups had no semantic parent association.             | Each expanded row owns its mounted child group with a unique ID.                                  | WCAG 1.3.1: expose the visible parent/child relationship to assistive technology. |
| MEDIUM   | `FileTree.tsx:146`, `ui/primitives/tree.tsx:77` | Expand-only folders declared an unselected selectable state. | Folders omit selection state; selectable files and generic selectable branches retain false/true. | WCAG 4.1.2: reflect the control's actual supported state.                         |

### Tree entry after directory Retry

Actual Wails reproduced a continuation defect after the shared read-error handoff:
Retry focused the named Files tree, but ArrowDown left focus on that container.
Tab entered `apps`, where the same arrow reached `go.mod`. The keyboard primitive
requires a row target; the missing contract was entry into the composite, not a
second directory cursor or different retry policy.

`apps/web/src/ui/primitives/tree.tsx` now handles focus on the root itself. It
calls the supplied `onFocus` first and, only if that event remains unhandled and
the root still owns document focus, synchronously enters the existing
`[role="treeitem"][tabindex="0"]`. The root-refresh qualification below now
permits the browser to reveal an offscreen cursor during this explicit entry.
Descendant focus and a
caller's prevented or redirected focus remain authoritative. Without a cursor,
focus stays on the root. The primitive neither chooses a first/selected row nor
activates an item. `FileTree` retains its one cursor owner, while selected-file
memory, directory expansion, data requests, file reading and Composer retain
their existing owners. Completion does not move focus.

The [WAI tree pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/) informs
row keyboard navigation and the distinction between focus and selection.
Read-only ZCode row/list implementations confirm row-owned keyboard actions and
named tree scope; their every-row tab stops are a different model, not evidence
for Flame's retry restoration. The better-accessibility focus/keyboard guidance
informs preserving the current task and later input. Existing typography, quiet
surfaces, semantic tokens and focus treatment remain unchanged.

### Root file-list refresh continuity

Actual Wails at `454cd3b9e` reproduced a separate failure: after opening and
returning from `reading-guide.md`, move the cursor to unselected `README.md` and
refresh the root listing. The query still retained all six accepted entries when
the request failed, but `DataView` replaced the entire FileTree; document focus
became BODY and the local cursor disappeared. The lost owner was the mounted
browser projection, not the cached list or Runtime filesystem data.

`FileWorkspace.tsx` now retains that same FileTree only while the current query
has accepted nonempty data. Failure and retry feedback occupy the existing
`WorkspaceViewLayout.notice` slot outside its scrollport, so recovery remains
visible while browsing the list. A compact loading state replaces Retry while
the request is pending. Initial failure, an accepted empty list, workspace
resolution and a different CWD retain their ordinary replacement semantics.
No last-good copy, query-policy change, second cursor or deferred focus action
is introduced.

`DataError` now owns the existing unsupported-method classification for both
ordinary `DataView` errors and retained refresh feedback. Unsupported calls keep
the warning presentation and no Retry; transport failures remain recoverable.
An optional DOM `focusTarget` lets the retiring, currently focused Retry enter
its surviving sibling tree. Existing callers keep their nearest focusable-host
handoff. Other focus is left alone, and the callback still receives no DOM event.
`FileTree` forwards that native ref; the primitive enters its existing cursor
with ordinary browser focus so an offscreen row can be revealed.

The first native candidate exposed a further layout defect: at 18 px with 31
rendered rows, the new error block displaced focused `review-24.md` outside the
viewport, and preventing scroll on explicit tree entry left it offscreen.
`FileBrowserLayout` uses React's pre-mutation snapshot to retain only the active
row that was fully visible before an update. If that same connected row still
owns focus and is newly occluded after layout, it scrolls nearest without moving
focus. An already scrolled-away row or later draft focus does not qualify.
The class has no state, observer, timer or duplicate layout model. The feedback
slot keeps the recovery action outside the scrolling rows.

Read-only ZCode's `workspace-file-tree/WorkspaceFileTree.tsx` distinguishes an
accepted root from a blocking first error; its cached-error toast supports the
nonblocking task model, not Flame's focus or persistence implementation. Flame
uses its existing query cache and persistent in-pane recovery. The
[WAI keyboard guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/)
and [tree pattern](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/) inform
visible focus, composite entry and separate selection. React's
[pre-mutation snapshot contract](https://react.dev/reference/react/Component#getsnapshotbeforeupdate)
provides the DOM lifecycle needed to distinguish displacement from prior user
scrolling. The better-accessibility, typography and writing guidance applies to
this complete browse/recover/read/return flow; existing tokens, surfaces,
Flame Orange, custom accent ownership and font roles remain unchanged.

### Long-file targets and prepend ownership

The persistent file reader keeps the file's identity, line range and navigation
beside the conversation. Loading another range of the same file preserves the
previous content, but that placeholder cannot settle the new navigation request.
`FileWorkspace.tsx` passes a null placement intent to `FileView.tsx` until the
current query has accepted content. `FileView` then places that intent once.
Prepending captures the exact requested `LineWindow` with its height anchor; a
later window or navigation retires the anchor. The existing viewer, query and DOM
scrollport remain the owners. No per-file position cache, retry, delayed focus,
new state machine or shared-component override is added.

### Keep reading after file-range expansion

`FilePreview` in `FileWorkspace.tsx` owns the lifetime of the earlier/later range
actions. Before either action changes its existing `LineWindow`, it transfers
focus to the existing named scrollport only if that exact button currently owns
focus. `preventScroll` preserves placement while the existing prepend anchor or
append path handles content geometry. The rule also applies when the action
remains available after expansion. There is no focus action on query completion,
so later typing or navigation keeps its focus. Shared controls, query identity,
file navigation, target placement and Runtime semantics are unchanged.

Actual Wails reproduced the defect on unchanged `11d9712b7`: from lines
**100–500**, keyboard activation of the earlier action accepted **1–500** and
removed the focused button, leaving focus on `BODY`. Page Down did nothing at
**1,848 px / lines 97–137**. The next Tab jumped to the remaining action at
**8,791 px**. Loading the final lines similarly removed its focused action,
leaving `BODY` at **8,758 px / lines 461–501** with Page Down ineffective.

The better-accessibility focus guidance and
[WAI keyboard-interface guidance](https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/#kbd_focus_discernable_predictable)
support transferring focus to a logical surviving destination when a focused
control can disappear. Flame already has that destination and uses the same
local ownership principle in retiring error actions. Read-only ZCode code-viewer
research concerns request-scoped placement and preserved scrolling, not Flame's
focus rule. Existing better-series layout, typography, colors and control
surfaces remain intact; no component library or new semantic token is introduced.

## Dock tab task continuity

`apps/web/src/ui/agent/context-dock.tsx` keeps tab selection and close/reorder
commands with their existing host owners. Its local post-action focus intent now
captures the actual document origin and the affected tab's live popup. Only a tab,
that popup or an unclaimed body can initiate settlement. The existing frame
boundary respects later focus, including another tab, and ignores disconnected
destinations. A closing popup can still finish its own focus entry before that
frame without being mistaken for an unrelated choice. Popup identity is derived
from the rendered tab ID, without a shared ref competing across menu lifetimes.

The existing tab list prevents only middle-button mousedown's focus transfer;
primary pressing, Base UI activation, overflow and drag/drop retain their owners.
Middle-closing a background tab therefore keeps a surviving Composer or reader
control and its text/selection context. A removed focused tab settles on the
surviving active tab, or the available header return/Browse action when none
remains. Delete/Backspace also respect an already consumed key and the existing
shared `isImeKey` contract, including legacy 229. No new tab state, global listener,
timer, geometry, theme or command policy was introduced.

Read-only research inspected ZCode's actual `SidePaneTabTrigger.tsx` and
`AnimatedSidePanePanel.tsx` for background closure and contextual actions. Its
custom-div/all-pointer policy was not copied into Flame's native Base UI buttons.
Installed Base UI 1.9.0 explicitly permits secondary-press focus without
selection, which is a different fact from continued authoring focus. HeroUI's
local overflow Tabs example and prior Radix tab/focus references inform the
composite and overflow model rather than a new close lifecycle. ChatGPT's actual
side-panel source remains evidence for separate material identity; it is not
native close-focus proof. Better-series review retains current type, semantic
surfaces, Orange/custom-blue focus and the same workbench composition. Static
Ace references supply no keyboard evidence.

## Retained workspace and result views

The native Memory query reset had two host causes. Activity hide disconnected
`RenderingComponent`'s external-store subscription, ending the captured context;
composition Effect cleanup also retired resolved descendants. Main and Dock
placements separately rendered the same view. Preserving only a search value
would have left drafts and original mutation retry closures attached to retired
contexts.

`ChatPanel.tsx` now renders one keyed body per exact Session/view ID. Its existing
Dock tabs, active main view and distinct main sources on the inspection chain
supply retention; there is no second state cache. A same-view return shortcut
cannot keep a closed moved tab alive. `PanelHost` marks surrounding view identity
and changes only its closed `density` value between page and compact presentation,
preserving the same children. The stable Dock container is neutral and non-focusable in main
mode; the named body and persistent window header keep their roles, and main
content does not inherit Dock containment/clipping.

Conversation results and retained delegated readers use the same mounted-tree
policy. `packages/ui/src/content-visibility.tsx` projects inherited presentation visibility
without state, cancellation or I/O. `MessageStream` preserves the public follow
library's two DOM wrappers and viewport class, attaching its measuring refs only
while visible. `ChatStream` suspends only its Composer geometry observer, and
`SubagentTranscript` combines ancestor and local visibility. This matters in real
WebKit: retained hidden readers otherwise measured zero and jumped to the bottom.
No scroll-position cache or replacement business lifetime was added.

Native page zoom while a retained reader is hidden has a separate limit. On
macOS 26.5, changing 150% to 200% while its ancestor is `hidden` changed a
777,329 CSS-pixel position to 582,997 on return. A plain HTML scroller reproduced
the exact change without React, virtualization, ResizeObserver or application
scroll handlers. Ordinary hide/show at unchanged zoom retained 777,329, and visible
zoom retained that same position. This is not evidence of another component
lifetime or virtual-window defect. The [WebKit scroll-area implementation](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebCore/rendering/RenderLayerScrollableArea.cpp)
saves and restores a layer position; [the DOM scroll getter](https://github.com/WebKit/WebKit/blob/main/Source/WebCore/dom/Element.cpp)
removes the current zoom. A saved layer offset restored under a different scale
is consistent with the observed 150/200 ratio. That is a source-based explanation,
not identification of the exact installed system WebKit revision. Keep this
limitation explicit rather than adding a competing application scroll cache or
keeping every hidden workspace laid out solely for this edge case.

`useInspectionFocus.ts` gives a removed layout trigger's focus to the presented
main body, visible Dock or conversation only when focus fell to the document
body. Existing explicit source returns and later outside focus keep priority.
Actual tab removal, main-only replacement, exact Session/target replacement and
resource/contribution retirement retain their cancellation behavior. Runtime,
receipts, bindings, SDK and portable component sources are unchanged.

Reference evidence: ZCode's read-only `AnimatedSidePanePanel.tsx` retains actual
tab content with `forceMount` plus inactive hiding and explicit visibility for
owned side-pane work. ChatGPT's actual `ReviewThreadSidePanelTab` separates its
review state from the portal target; it is not export-renderer evidence. The
[React Activity contract](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity) documents
Effect cleanup on hide; [Radix Tabs](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/tabs)
provides the semantic reference for persistent tab content. Flame retains its
Base UI/StyleX owners. The better-layout/accessibility review drove instance,
measurement, landmark and focus boundaries; existing typography, writing and
semantic color owners were checked in both native themes without a palette or
prose redesign.

### Recorded output Find navigation

The complete reply → recorded command → expanded output → Find → manual reading
→ Find again → close/collapse → continue the original draft path is accepted.
Native Wails reproduced a real failure on the frozen source: a unique match first
appeared at scrollTop 639, but after scrolling to 2437, Enter, Shift+Enter and a
refined query selecting that same line all left it outside the rendered window.
Find kept saying 1 of 1 and retained input focus, so that count did not mean the
requested evidence had been revealed.

**Cause and implementation**

`plugins/tool-results/component/recorded-output.tsx:140` replaces independent
query and match state with one local Find value. Each explicit query/navigation
action publishes a new value, including an unchanged index. The existing reveal
effect at line 220 observes that value and the source/row geometry. Matching,
selected-line highlighting and the accessible counter derive from the same owner.
Manual scrolling updates only viewport geometry and does not request a jump.
No-match, Clear, Close/Escape and collapse retain their established behavior.
The existing FindField composition guards, preview, virtualization, text/copy,
styles, captured-result identity and Runtime boundaries are unchanged. No new
counter, focus handler, cache, timer or retry is added. The component README
records the contract and the normal plugin builder updates its shipped ESM.

Read-only ZCode `v4/useConversationTimelineFind.ts` separates the selected match
from its explicit navigation request when revealing a range. That evidence and
better-accessibility's keyboard scope/return rules guide the behavior; Flame
keeps its existing local Find and shared controls rather than copying ZCode's
larger navigation model.

from `shell/workbench/panel/readingColumn.ts` to its logical home beside the

since those belong to the shell that owns the floating composer, not to message
rendering. Shell consumers (`MessageStream`, `ChatStream`, `FloatingComposer`)
import the axis through the chat public surface — the same direction by which the
shell now consumes `MessageTranscript`.

The earlier move repaired the dependency direction but left an incomplete
composition: `SubagentsPanel` used the capped box without its gutter. Actual
Wails showed an 808 px inner body where the main reader had 768 px; padding on
the outside scroller did not repair that contract. The shared transcript now
applies `readingColumn.gutter` to every turn, date separator and turn fallback,
inside the host's `readingColumn.box`. The child summary and empty state compose
the same gutter separately. Its local
`--reading-gutter` projects the existing `--layout-compact-gutter`, preserving the
narrow Dock's inset. The overview list keeps that same token on its scroller;

## Empty, error and unsupported state ownership

The empty/error/unsupported distinction is now owned once. `EmptyState`
(`packages/ui`) gained a `tone` that colors the icon mark through the existing
`Tone` vocabulary, so a failure reads as a failure instead of relying on each
caller to remember an alert glyph. `IconMark` maps the tone to the shared badge
surfaces; its default stays the accent mark, so existing empties are unchanged.
`DataView` renders its error branch with `tone="negative"` and its unsupported
branch with `tone="warning"`, which covers every list screen in one place.

Four sites that bypassed `DataView` and conflated states were corrected:
`SubagentsPanel`'s unavailable run and `ApprovalsPane`'s load failure were
rendering an error as a neutral empty — the same icon as "nothing here" and no
retry — and now use the alert glyph with the negative tone, with Approvals
offering a retry. `HooksPane` dropped its hand-rolled unsupported branch and
routes that state through `DataView`'s `unsupported` config, removing the
duplicate. `ToolControls` uses the shared recovery surface; its local titles now
name tool visibility, auto-approve rules and the tools list so their independent
retries remain understandable.

The original shared-tone verification rebuilt `@flame/ui`, passed its 74 tests
and the then-current 3,069-test Web suite. Current native acceptance below
qualifies negative failure, warning unsupported and ordinary empty presentation

## Wide-content breakout in the reading band

Actual Wails on `955cfb690` exposed the missing boundary in the original broad
`.md` descendant rule. Expanded user code and images escaped the narrower user
bubble; quote, list and Callout code borrowed the conversation pane's width and
put actions behind the Dock or outside their local surface. The width formula
was not the owner of eligibility.

`BlockRenderer` now marks its existing text wrapper with
`data-slot="message-text"`. `markdown.css` grants breakout only through the
observed outer assistant text chain:
`.msg-content:not([data-user-message-bubble]) > [data-block-anchor] > [data-slot="message-text"] > .md`.
Only direct code, media, Mermaid frames and display math inside a direct paragraph
take the wide width. Direct table containers take only `max-width`, preserving
intrinsic narrow tables. User bubbles, nested Markdown, list/quote/Callout content,
reasoning and NarrativeWave text keep their local boundary. No wrapper, clipping,
measurement, new state or event workaround was added.

The existing 640–1151.98 px `conversation` container band, left-anchored growth,
56rem cap and width formula remain:
`max(100%, min(var(--wide-column-max), 100cqi - max(0px, (100cqi - var(--reading-column-max)) / 2) - 2 * var(--reading-gutter-wide)))`.
The complete subagent column composition above makes that geometry apply to the
same owned axis in a full pane and a widened Dock. Ordinary code, table and media
scrolling, selection, typography, radius, theme and Runtime owners are unchanged.
The better-layout, better-typography and better-accessibility guidance informs
stable grouping, reading measure and reachable local operations; it does not
justify a second component system or global theme change.

not a claim about a particular platform preference or every scroll input.

clipboard primitives, extension action contracts, command lifecycle, Runtime,
reader selection and Toaster presentation remain unchanged. Both new keys are

### Reading focus through geometry changes

A previously visible keyboard control now stays within its reading viewport when
native resize, page zoom or content reflow changes that viewport. The main and
selected subagent transcripts share `useReadingFocusVisibility` beside the
existing focus/disclosure policies in `ui/agent/readingFollow.ts`. CSS remains
the authority for Composer and jump-control clearance; no per-Tool offset is added.

The attached visible viewport retains only its pre-change safe frame and visible
active descendant. WebKit's geometry-induced scroll can precede ResizeObserver;
that event defers re-witnessing until the new frame is observed. Ordinary scroll
re-witnesses actual visibility, including nested evidence clipping, while a wheel
gesture retires the witness immediately. Geometry can move only the owned viewport
and only for the same still-focused, rendered descendant. Existing follow stops
before that adjustment. Native integer scroll offsets require outward ceil/floor
rounding; a **0.5 CSS px** measurement tolerance handles fractional zoom edges.
There is no focus call, activation, retry, timer, extra follow state or ancestor
scroll. Hidden/detached readers disconnect through their existing visibility lifetime.

Read-only ZCode `packages/ui/src/v4/timelineScrollAnchor.ts` reconciles user intent
before content anchoring, illustrating why user scrolling wins over a later
measurement. Its virtualizer/follow model is not copied. Existing actual ChatGPT
disclosure and HeroUI accordion research informs reading ownership; the six
better-* domains are reviewed against this concrete task.
